warnings.why: Compensation of employees typically accounts for around 10 to 12 percent of GDP and a much larger share of general government expenses (often over 30-40%), making 6.58% implausibly low for public employee pay share of expenses.

Germany's general government compensation of employees as a share of total expenses is historically around 25-30%. A figure of 5.72% is far too low and likely reflects a classification or data reporting error (e.g., using a narrow sub-sector of government).

In Spain, public sector wages represent a substantial portion of public expenditure, usually well above 20%. The reported value of 5.93% is abnormally low compared to standard macroeconomic statistics for the country.

General government spending on employee compensation in the Netherlands is normally around 20-25% of total expenses. A value of 7.81% strongly suggests a partial coverage or misclassification in the World Bank database.
Belgium has a large public sector with compensation of employees traditionally making up roughly 25% of government expenses. A value of 5.87% is implausibly low.

policy: model memory is advisory; unsupported suspicions cannot overrule official data
